transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, thank you for coming in today. I have some information to share with you regarding your previous imaging scans, and it is something that is difficult to talk about.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything alright, Doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not exactly. When we reviewed your records, we found a mistake. There was a small finding on your scan from last year that needed a follow-up appointment in three months. This note was placed in a part of the report that the primary team didn't see, so that follow-up was never scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. A mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to process. To put it simply, the radiologist saw something that needed a second look, but because of how the report was written, that message didn't get to the people who schedule the appointments. It was missed. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are the doctor. I trusted that everything was being handled.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely reasonable to trust your medical team. Does it feel a bit overwhelming to hear that something was missed?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just... I feel very confused. I thought I was healthy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very unsettling feeling to realize the plan wasn't followed. I want to sit with you in this for a moment. There is no rush.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The information was documented in a sub-section of the report. It wasn't in the main summary, so the primary team didn't see it. It was a failure in how the information was passed along. To make sure I am being clear, do you understand why the appointment didn't happen?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. The paper was not read correctly. But what does this mean for me now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is the most important question. We need to address that finding now to see if it has changed or if it requires treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I have been waiting for a year.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how distressing this is for you, especially since you've been trusting us for a whole year without knowing this was pending.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it my fault for not asking more?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not at all. You did everything you were supposed to do. You came to your appointments and followed the directions you were given.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If this was a mistake, who is responsible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for forwarding reports failed in this instance. The notes were placed in a section that wasn't flagged for the clinical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel very shaken. I didn't expect this today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. This is a heavy thing to find out unexpectedly. We can just take a few minutes of silence if you need it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I want to know what happens next. I am worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That worry is completely valid. We are going to get this sorted out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will make sure the next steps are taken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What are those steps? Do I need a new scan tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look into getting a new imaging study ordered soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When exactly? Monday? Tuesday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see what the schedule looks like and we'll get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to wait again. I need a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand the urgency. We will keep an eye on the system and someone will likely send an email or a letter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A letter? I want to know for sure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for a notification from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the doctor who missed it? Will they be the one doing the new scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a documentation error in the report. We'll just make sure the current team handles the next scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I cannot trust the papers anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see why you'd feel that way. When the record doesn't match the care you received, it breaks that trust.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do I do now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: For now, you just need to wait for us to coordinate the new appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How do I know it won't be missed again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are aware of the issue now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But how? Give me a reason to believe it won't happen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just be more careful with the reports moving forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will go home and think about this. I feel very uneasy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this isn't the news you expected, and it's okay to feel uneasy. We'll be in touch.

H.justification: Resident allows for silence, never interrupts, and remains regulated even when the patient expresses distrust and urgency.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language, checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense so far?', 'do you understand why...'), and avoided false reassurance.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') was used, and responsibility was deflected to 'the system' and 'documentation error'.

R.justification: Resident specifically named emotions ('overwhelming', 'unsettling', 'distressing', 'shaken', 'uneasy') and engaged with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan consists entirely of placeholders ('we'll see what the schedule looks like', 'stay tuned', 'someone will likely send an email') with no specific timeline or patient role.
